"Blow the shofar at the new moon," etc. (Tehillim 81:4).
דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא קָרִיב לוֹן לְגַבֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵּי,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, draws them near to Himself, etc.,
and from a distant place He drew them near to Himself.
'And Yehoshua said to all the people,

to show that from a distant place
הָנֵי קְרָאֵי אִית לְאִסְתַּכָּלָא בְּהוּ וְכוּלֵּי,
These verses need to be looked into, etc.
Rather, certainly, the hidden meaning of the matter is:
טִיבוּ סַגֵּי עָבֵיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
the Holy One, blessed be He, did a great kindness
with Yisrael, in that He chose them through the Avos, etc.,
וְאַפֵּיק לוֹן מִגּוֹ נַהֲרָא עִלָּאָה וְכוּלֵּי,
and brought them out from within the supernal river, etc.
כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ בְּעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר וְכוּלֵּי,
'Thus says Hashem: beyond the river,' etc.
מֵעוֹלָם — מַאי קָא בָּעֵי הָכָא וְכוּלֵּי,
'from of old' — what is it doing here? etc.
אֶלָּא הַהוּא נָהָר עוֹלָם אִיקְרֵי וְכוּלֵּי.
Rather, that river is called 'olam,' etc."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח, א)
This accords with what they said (Sanhedrin 38a)
she has hewn out her seven pillars":
זוֹ מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
this is the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁבָּרָא אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בְּחָכְמָה.
Who created the entire world with wisdom."
These are the attributes that the Holy One, blessed be He,
emanated for the creation of the world:
and Binah is called by the name "Imma," Mother.
For in the Holy One, blessed be He,
in His essence and His very being,
there is no grasp at all and no name at all;
only in the attributes that Hashem, may He be blessed, emanated
for the creation of the world
do we describe Chochmah and Binah
by the names Abba and Imma,
and they are what give birth to the other attributes.
וּבִינָה עָלְמָא דְאָתֵי (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קנח, א),
And Binah is the World to Come (Zohar II 158a);
ה׳ — בִּינָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רלב, א).
the letter hei is Binah (Zohar III 232a).
"This world was created with the letter hei,
and the World to Come with the letter yud."
And this is "from a distant place He chose them,"
דְּאַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא אָב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for Avraham is called the first father of Yisrael,
since all the nations are called the children of Noach,
except to Avraham, who is the first father
who was born in the holiness of Yisrael;
"'When they were created,' behibaram — through Avraham."
וְהָיָה גַּם כֵּן מֵאֲתַר רְחִיקָא, מִבִּינָה.
And he too was from "a distant place," from Binah.
"She has hewn out her seven pillars" —
these are the seven days of Creation (Sanhedrin ibid.),
which correspond to the seven shepherds,
who are a chariot for the seven attributes,
as they said in the holy Zohar
Now, the connection of this opening
and likewise in the holy Zohar —
why did he open with this
for the subject of blowing the shofar?
that they should accept the Torah willingly.
שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה אִיתָא (שַׁבָּת פח, א)
For concerning the time of Matan Torah it says (Shabbos 88a):
"From here there is a great protest against the Torah."
So Yehoshua wanted to bring them into a covenant
in which they would accept willingly,
since what they accepted in the days of Moshe
so that He would bring them into Eretz Yisrael
אַךְ אֵצֶל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָיָה גַּם כֵּן
But with Yehoshua, too, it was
on account of the love of the Land,
for he had brought them into Eretz Yisrael.
"They accepted it anew in the days of Achashverosh,"
for then they accepted it out of love,
since nothing new at all had come about for them
except that the decree was annulled;
but they still remained in exile,
Therefore the acceptance then was out of love.
And because of this Yehoshua mentioned
that the beginning of the choosing
who was the first father of Yisrael.
וָאֶתֵּן לְיִצְחָק אֶת יַעֲקֹב וְאֶת עֵשָׂו,
and I gave to Yitzchak Yaakov and Esav":
for Hashem, may He be blessed, took everything "from of old"
and created all the souls of the Avos
Even regarding Esav the expression of giving is used,
שֶׁהָיָה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר
for he too was called an apostate Yisrael
and there were in him holy sparks
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
that it alludes to the soul of Rabbi Meir,
to uproot the name Yisrael from himself.
And Yehoshua mentioned to them "from a distant place,"
from there He brought the Avos,
who are the root of the Written Torah.
שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ט, א),
the two thousand years of Torah (Avodah Zarah 9a),
וְקִיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ (יוֹמָא כח, ב).
and he kept the entire Torah (Yoma 28b).
according to what they said in the holy Zohar
"The Torah comes from the side of Gevurah."
And Yaakov is the aspect of truth,
which are called Abba and Imma,
are what gave birth to the Avos,
who were the root of the Written Torah;
and so too the creation of the world
As for the matter of blowing the shofar,
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז, ב דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל כְּדֵי)
in the name of the Yerushalmi,
"And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar shall be blown":
"When the Satan hears the sound of the shofar
once, he is alarmed and yet not alarmed;
and when he hears it a second time
he says, 'Surely this is the shofar of
and my time has come to be swallowed up,'
and he is thrown into confusion," etc.
that the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,
and that this mitzvah is fulfilled every year
is also an enactment of the Sages;
so why is he thrown into confusion
אַךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רסו, ב)
But in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 266b)
the attribute of Binah is called "the great shofar,"
and it is the aspect of "Binah is the heart"
that it enters into the depths of the heart.
And the shofar is the arousal
of dread and awe of Hashem, may He be blessed,
"Shall a shofar be blown in a city
when it becomes fixed in the heart forever,
so that it is never again forgotten;
for this is the meaning of "great":
And it is written "a great shofar shall be blown,"
and it is not written who blows it,
"And Hashem Elokim will blow the shofar."
Rather, the whole intent of the shofar-blowing
is to arouse the great shofar,
which is an arousal in the depths of the heart,
as it will be in the future,
as it says, "And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar shall be blown,
and the lost shall come," etc.,
for through this will be aroused
even the lost and the cast away.
so that from above there enters
the arousal into the depths of the heart.
he is alarmed and yet not alarmed":
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הִתְעוֹרְרוּת,
that is, even though this too is an arousal,
therefore he is not so alarmed.
and the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
that comes to rectify "the abundance of anger" —
he says, "Surely this is the shofar of
the great shofar will be aroused
to become fixed in the depths of the heart,
and through this "his time has come
to be swallowed up," and he is thrown into confusion,
he has no time to make accusation.
the main purpose of the exiles among the nations
is to bring out "what they swallowed from their mouths" —
whatever is found in them, too,
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh;
there will be the ingathering of the exiles,
"If they all study, now I will gather them."
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא הַמִּשְׁנָה,
And the root of Torah she'b'al peh is the Mishnah,
'and of the fat of the earth' (ibid.) — this is Mishnah."
And perhaps this is alluded to
in what Yitzchak said to Esav (ibid. 27:39):
"Behold, of the fat of the earth shall be your dwelling";
in the name of the Arizal
on the verse "for game was in his mouth,"
that it refers to the soul of Rabbi Meir.
a root of Torah she'b'al peh,
דִּסְתָם מִשְׁנָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר (סַנְהֶדְרִין פו, א),
for an unattributed Mishnah is Rabbi Meir (Sanhedrin 86a),
and the root of Torah she'b'al peh
is the Mishnah, as was said.
the root of Torah she'b'al peh,

because he "enlightened the eyes of the Sages in halachah"
fathom the full depth of his reasoning,
This is the meaning of what they said
in the name of the Aruch (entry Arav):
that the hundred sounds of the shofar-blowing
And presumably it is found in some Midrash,
that she cried out a hundred sounds,
since it is cited in the Aruch.
of the shofar-blowing have to do
with the wailings of Sisera's mother?
but to set a hundred sounds
what reason is there in this?
But it accords with what we said
that they needed a war from Heaven,
And we explained it according to what is found
(מַאֲמַר חִקּוּר דִּין חֵלֶק ה פֶּרֶק יא)
that Rabbi Akiva descended from Sisera,
שֶׁבָּא עַל יָעֵל אֵשֶׁת חֶבֶר הַקֵּנִי.
who came upon Yael, the wife of Chever the Keini.
שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
the root of Torah she'b'al peh, as mentioned above,
and Yael drew it out of him —
the wife of Chever the Keini,
for the Keinim too had their portion
in the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is the matter of "the fertile land of Yericho"
that was given to them, as is known.
And for this the war had
to be "from heaven the stars fought,"
so that they could bring out
which is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
that was in exile with Sisera
And it is written of Yael (Shoftim 5:24):
"Above women in the tent she shall be blessed,"
"Who are the women in the tent?
from whom the Avos came forth,
שֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
who were the root of the Written Torah, as mentioned above;
and she brought forth the soul of Rabbi Akiva.
And with this their life came to an end,
for this had been the essence of their life,
"And You give life to them all."
That is why she cried out a hundred sounds,
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה אָנוּ תּוֹקְעִין מֵאָה קוֹלוֹת,
and corresponding to this we blow a hundred sounds,
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh.
And the number one hundred indicates
דְּמָצִינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ אַרְבָּעִים וָתֵשַׁע פָּנִים לַתּוֹרָה
For we find that there are forty-nine facets to the Torah
at the start of Parshas Chukas, 19:2),
And there are seventy facets to the Torah
meaning that when each attribute is comprised
And one hundred is ultimate completeness:
when all ten attributes are comprised,
And in the kelipah, "one opposite the other":
when the spark of the aspect
מִבְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
of Torah she'b'al peh was with him, as mentioned above,
therefore his mother cried out a hundred sounds.
And this is what they said in the Yerushalmi:
"When he hears it a second time
he says, 'Surely this is the shofar of
the great shofar will be aroused,
"If they all study, now I will gather them."
And the great shofar, which is Binah, will be aroused,
so that it remains engraved in the heart
and all "the abundance of anger" will be rectified,
and "his time has come to be swallowed up,"
and there will be the true rectification,
as it says, "And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar shall be blown," etc.
And this is the meaning of the verse (Tehillim 89:16):
"Fortunate is the people that know the teruah,"
"Do the nations not know how to sound a teruah?
How many horns they have!" etc.
that through the action below they arouse
which will bring the true rectification:
death will be swallowed up forever,
all the damage will be repaired,
along with the blemish of the serpent,
and it will be as before the blemish,
And this is "Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they walk,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רלא, ב)
"In the light of the countenance of the Holy One, blessed be He —
and this is the primordial light
that the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away for the tzaddikim,"
which is the light of Torah she'b'al peh;
the light that was created on the first day,
which the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away
for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh," etc.
And this is the meaning of this opening
for the blowing of the shofar.
